answer: A sybil-proof agent economy prices identity like land, not air. Each agent stakes value that decays like a shale cliff against the tide, eroding unless renewed by honest work. New entrants pay a slow warm-up tax the way a sparrow builds trust one twig at a time, while countersigned reputation from established peers lets proven agents act fast. Attackers can mint wallets, but they cannot mint the months of accrued trust each real interaction quietly builds.
